sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Center tile: N→g→N. So the center cycles between g↔N (two states). The plus tiles cycle between W↔N. The bottom tile: W↔N, and g is special.
So the tiles don't cycle to g (except for the center). The plus tiles are stuck in the W/N loop. The bottom tile can never return to g except via a reset.
So then, how did the bottom tile become g at t22/29/33/46? Via a reset from a previous size-toggle click. The chain: initial state all g → click bottom (g) → toggle + reset to all g → click bottom (g) → toggle + reset...
So as long as I don't click any tile, I can freely toggle the size! The moment I click a plus tile, it becomes W or N and can never return to g → the size toggle is locked forever (until the timer runs out?).
Damn. I've already broken the bottom tile (now W). The size is locked at 4×4.
However... it's different if the timer reset restores everything. The W bar on the right side is a timer. When it runs out: game over, or a level reset?
Or maybe I'm wrong about the trigger. Let me re-verify: is the trigger "bottom=g", or is it "bottom=g AND L=R=N"? At t22/29/33/46, L=R=N. This time L=R=W → no toggle. If the trigger is L=N AND R=N (regardless of the bottom's state), then I can set L=N, R=N (one click each: W→N), and then click the bottom (W→N, and if L=R=N then the toggle fires?).
This is a testable hypothesis! Current: T=W, L=W, R=W, B=W, C=N.
Plan: click L (W→N), click R (W→N), click B (W→N). Observe whether the size toggles.
If the size toggles → 2×2! Then dock it in the hole.
If it doesn't toggle, the hypothesis is dead; in that case, wait for the timer reset or look for another mechanism.
Let me execute this 3-click sequence.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def plus(fr):
    res={}
    for name,(r,c) in {'T':(50,30),'L':(55,25),'R':(55,35),'B':(60,30),'C':(55,30)}.items():
        for n in fr.segmentation['nodes']:
            bb=n['boundary']
            r0=min(p[0] for p in bb); c0=min(p[1] for p in bb)
            if abs(r0-r)<=1 and abs(c0-c)<=1:
                res[name]=n['color']
    return res
def size(fr):
    tot=0
    for n in fr.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color'] in ('b','S') and n['pixels']>=2:
            bb=n['boundary']
            r0=min(p[0] for p in bb); c0=min(p[1] for p in bb)
            if r0>=17 and c0>16: tot+=n['pixels']
    return tot
print('before:', plus(current_frame), 'size', size(current_frame))
r = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':55,'col':25}])
print('after L:', plus(history[-1].frame), 'size', size(history[-1].frame))
r = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':55,'col':35}])
print('after R:', plus(history[-1].frame), 'size', size(history[-1].frame))
r = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':60,'col':30}])
print('after B:', plus(history[-1].frame), 'size', size(history[-1].frame), 'changed:', r.get('board_changed'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
